1. Heard learned counsel appearing for the applicant and learned APP for the State.

Despite service,
none appears for non-applicant No.2.
Admit.
Heard finally by consent.

2. By this application, the applicant is seeking quashing of FIR in connection with Crime No.631/2023 registered with non-applicant No.1 police station for offences under Sections 376,
376(2)(n), 417, and 506 of the IPC and consequent proceeding arising out of the same bearing chargesheet No.132/2023 and RCC No.278/2023.
3.

The crime is registered on the basis of a report lodged by non-applicant No.2 (the complainant),
who is 42 years lady, on allegations that the applicant used to visit her house as there was friendship between him and her husband.
On 6.8.2015, her husband died.
Thereafter, on various occasions, the applicant used to visit her house and enquire her as to whether she is suffering from any difficulty.
She has further alleged that on 5.8.202, the applicant visited her house.
At that time, her son, aged 17 years, was present in the house and the applicant promised her that he will provide an employment to her son and also provide some grocery articles.
She has further alleged that at the relevant time, she along with the applicant were only present in the house and he has promised her for marriage.
On the promise of marriage, he subjected her for forceful sexual assault.
It is further alleged by her that, thereafter, on various occasions, he has subjected her for forceful sexual assault and this was continued upto May 2020.
Thereafter, the applicant also promised her that he will give her some agricultural land as well as house.
On that count also, he has subjected her for forceful sexual assault and the last incident she has narrated is dated 14.8.2023 when the applicant took her to hospital.
On the basis of the said report, the police have registered the crime against the present applicant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that recital of the FIR itself shows that relationship between the applicant and the complainant was consensual in nature.

He has invited my attention towards various statements of witnesses including statement of son of the complainant and submitted that there is no proximity between misconception of fact and the alleged incident of sexual assault as the relationship was continued for more than three years.
In view of that, he prayed for quashing of the FIR.

Learned APP for the State has strongly opposed the said contentions and submitted that considering, that under misconception of fact, her consent was obtained and, thereafter, the applicant has provided her a rented room and sexually exploited her, a prima facie case is made out against .....5/-
Judgment 18 apl1603.23 the applicant and, therefore, the application deserves to be rejected.
6.
On hearing both sides and perusing the entire investigation papers, it shows that there is no dispute that the complainant was acquainted with the applicant.
The relationship between the applicant and the complainant was continued from 5.8.2020 till 14.8.2023.

Recital of the FIR and statement of the complainant show that on the promise of marriage, the applicant has subjected her for forceful sexual assault and, thereafter, he has denied to perform the marriage with the complainant.

7. Thus, from recital of the FIR as well as statement of the complainant, it reveals that out of acquaintance, they were communicating with each other and, thereafter, physical relationship was developed between them.
.....6/-
Judgment 18 apl1603.23 8.
As far as misconception fact is concerned, there is no proximity in time as the relationship was continued for more than three years.
9. Recital of the FIR and contents of the statement of the complainant reveal that it was a consensual relationship between the applicant and the complainant.
10. The complainant, who is 42 years lady, cannot be said to have acted under the alleged false promise given by the applicant and under the misconception of fact.
Admittedly, the complainant herself is a married woman having a son of 17 years.

It is difficult to accept that she has acted under the alleged false promise given by the applicant or under the misconception of fact while giving the consent to have sexual relationship with the applicant.

11. This aspect is considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the celebrated judgment in the case of Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra and anr, reported in (2019)9 .....7/-
Judgment 18 apl1603.23 SCC 608.

Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra and anr, reported in (2019)9 .....7/-
Judgment 18
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court, after considering catena of decisions,
held that, "to summarize the legal position that emerges from the above cases, the "consent" of a woman with respect to Section 375 must involve an active and reasoned deliberation towards the proposed act.
To establish whether the "consent" was vitiated by a "misconception of fact" arising out of a promise to marry, two propositions must be established.
The promise of marriage must have been a false promise, given in bad faith and with no intention of being adhered to at the time it was given.

The false promise itself must be of immediate relevance, or bear a direct nexus to the Shrikrushna S/O Madadeorao Sakharkar vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Karanja (Lad) ... on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140396330/
3 woman's decision to engage in the sexual act".
12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The allegations in the FIR indicate that since 2020, the complainant, initially, entered into the said relationship and it was continued for more than three years.
13. Under Section 90 of the IPC, a "consent" given under a misconception of fact is not "consent" in the eyes of law.
Judgment 18 apl1603.23 But the misconception of fact has to be in proximity of time to the occurrence and cannot be spread over a period of four years.

It hardly needs any elaboration that the "consent" by the complainant was a conscious and informed choice made by her after due deliberation, it being spread over a long period of time coupled with a conscious positive action not to protest.

14. In view of the above legal position, if facts and circumstances of the present case are taken into consideration, the complainant, who is a grown up lady, aged about 42 years, has entered into the relationship after knowing consequences of her act and the relationship is consensual in nature.
15. In this view of the matter, the application deserves to be allowed.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass following order:
ORDER (1) The criminal application is allowed.

Application stands disposed of.
